method: Single OpenAI GPT-6 Astra-family assistant review; this reviewer previously authored the original-Q&A corpus and retrieval implementation and is not an independent human rater. Prior source familiarity is a limitation. During this review, only the public rubric, reviewer/samples.json and review-template.json were read; no private condition mapping, source-support packet, raw run or aggregate study report was inspected. Each candidate was compared with its supplied question, reference span and editorial context on the three frozen ordinal dimensions. Content score 1 is reserved for contradiction, 2 for mostly missing the reference position, 3 for partial alignment, 4 for close alignment, and 5 for the same substantive position. Wording evaluates rhetorical and sentence patterns; overlapping topic words or factual accuracy alone do not earn resemblance. Situation evaluates the visible conversational reaction, with null required if the supplied context cannot support a judgment. Editorial context is not an original preceding transcript, and no audio, delivery, emotional state or unseen context was assessed. Partial references are graded only against the supplied opening response, without assumptions about omitted continuation. Complete identity disclaimers are judged for interview-response similarity, not for the desirability of AI transparency. Incomplete generations would remain ungraded. Identical question/reference/context/completion state and identical candidate text receive identical scores; minor paraphrases can share an ordinal score. Notes paraphrase the comparison rather than reproducing original source wording. Factual support remains null pending a separate evidence-visible pass. These are subjective descriptive ratings by one model-assisted reviewer, not human validation, independent replication or a significance test.
